quote: I have a new a new addition I put on. I like to have that connected.
stewart_read: This is the customer's stated reason for the whole call — an existing solar owner wanting the new addition connected — and the rep files it with 'Okay. Awesome.' instead of building on it.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have intended to circle back once bill/kWh data was in hand, and did partially return to it at 04:24 with the satellite image detail.
coaching_implication: Reflect the addition back immediately: 'so this new addition is pulling power your existing system wasn't sized for — let's make sure the add-on covers that' ties the pitch to his stated motive from minute one.

quote: The last one the last one was 80 some dollars. One before that was $2.20 something, and the one for that was $2.30 something.
stewart_read: Customer just disclosed a bill that spiked into the $200+ range before dropping to $80 — a striking swing worth surfacing — but rep didn't reflect it, just kept pushing for a kWh figure.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the numbers too garbled to use cleanly given the customer's confused delivery, opting to wait for the actual bill via text instead.
coaching_implication: Even garbled, the rep could say 'that's a big jump — let's get the exact bill so we size the addition right,' turning confusion into forward motion instead of silently logging it.

quote: I don't want anything. And I have electric heat and air conditioning.
stewart_read: Electric heat and AC is a strong solar-fit signal (high consumption base) that the rep never acknowledges or uses to reinforce the value of an add-on system.
coaching_implication: Flag electric heat/AC explicitly as a reason the add-on makes sense — 'with electric heat and air, that addition's going to pull a lot more power, good thing we're looking at this now.'

quote: Do you remember, like, how many kilowatts it was?
stewart_read: Rep correctly recognized dollar figures alone aren't the design input needed and tried to get kWh, but customer couldn't provide it — the ask itself was right, follow-through (photo via text) was the correct fallback.
coaching_implication: Good instinct to seek the real number; next step should tie it back to the addition ('once we see the kWh with the new addition running, we'll know exactly what to add').

quote: We have two my my cleanup lady is gonna be here too. That won't be a problem, will it?
stewart_read: Customer raises a mild logistics worry; rep answers clearly that it's a phone call, resolving it in one line.
coaching_implication: Handled fine — no coaching gap here, included as evidence the rep can respond crisply when the ask is concrete.

quote: I'll just look out for your electric bill here in the next little bit if that's okay.
stewart_read: Appointment is booked but explicitly conditioned on the bill arriving by text — a real open loop, not just a soft-exit formality.
coaching_implication: This should be flagged prominently in the handoff — the design team needs the bill before Wednesday or the call risks going in without complete data.
